ex.en: My younger sibling keeps wearing my clothes.
I keep getting headaches lately.
My phone keeps turning off.
You shouldn't hit your little sibling.
My friend hit my shoulder as a joke.
The rain is beating hard against the window.

note: Used with -아/어도: 아무리 바빠도 'no matter how busy'.

ex.en: No matter how busy you are, you have to eat.
No matter how hard I look, I can't find my keys.
No matter how many times I call, they don't answer.

note: Usually 최선을 다하다 'to do one's best'.

ex.en: I did my best on the exam.
I'll do my best.
This is the best option for now.
What time do you usually get up?
Traffic is worse than usual today.
A cup of coffee, as usual, please.
The app won't install.
When is the air conditioner installer coming?
It took ten minutes to install the program.
My husband is a good cook.
I take a cooking class on weekends.
This restaurant is known for its Chinese food.
I was looking out the window.
The baby smiles as it looks at its mom.
Looking at the ocean calms me down.

note: Adverb 자세히 'in detail' is very common.

ex.en: Please explain in a bit more detail.
The map was detailed, so it was easy to find.
I'll text you the details.
Minho pretended to be asleep.
Don't pretend you don't know.
I only pretended to listen during the meeting.
I bought the train ticket in advance.
Two movie tickets, please.

ex.s: 이 표를 보면 일정이 다 나와요.
ex.en: This chart shows the whole schedule.
Don't lie.
The kid lied to their mom.
That's a lie, right?

note: Wake: 잠이 깨다, 잠에서 깨다. Break: 접시를 깨다.

ex.en: I woke up before dawn.

ex.s: 아기가 깨지 않게 조용히 해 주세요.
ex.en: Please be quiet so the baby doesn't wake up.
I broke a plate while doing the dishes.

note: For online videos, 영상 is more common.

ex.en: I'll show you the video I took yesterday.
The kids are watching a cartoon video.
I work out while watching a yoga video.
I've really gotten into drawing lately.
I tried it just for fun.
Have a fun trip!

en: to pull out; to pick, select

ex.en: I had a tooth pulled at the dentist.
I'll go take out some cash.
We picked our class president today.
This item is on sale.
When are new products coming in?
I ordered the product online.
The customer demanded a refund.
My company asks too much of me.
This job requires a lot of experience.

note: Bandage sense = Band-Aid; also called 반창고.

ex.en: My friend plays guitar in a band.
I'm going to my favorite band's concert this weekend.
Please put a bandage on my finger.
Where do you buy clothes like that?
I've never seen anyone like that.
I want to live in a house like that too.
Have you seen a black umbrella?
Black shoes suit you better.
The sky suddenly turned dark.
In the old days there were no shops in this neighborhood.
Grandma told me an old story.

ex.s: 이 노래 들으면 옛날 생각이 나요.
ex.en: This song reminds me of the old days.
Can you pick something off the menu for me?
Picking out a gift is the hardest part.
Choose whichever color you like.

en: to ignore; to look down on

ex.en: Ji-woo keeps ignoring my texts.
Just ignore that noise.
You shouldn't look down on people for their looks.
I'm really proud of my daughter.
I'm proud to be part of this team.
I want to be a son my parents are proud of.
Did you finish all your homework?
I finished work early today.
Let's end this conversation here.
My skin gets dry in winter.
You have really nice skin.
This cream is good for sensitive skin.
I'm not a good dancer.
Everyone danced together at the wedding.
I'm learning to dance these days.
Thanks for the explanation.
The teacher's explanations are easy to understand.
Read the instruction manual first.

note: 연결하다 = to connect; 연결되다 = to be connected.

ex.en: The Wi-Fi connection keeps dropping.
How do I connect to Bluetooth?
I'll connect you to the person in charge.
The kid refuses to take medicine.
The bank turned down my loan.
Kevin refused to have his picture taken.
This problem is a bit complicated.
The instructions are too complicated.
Downtown is crowded on weekends.
I need to update the software.
My company started using new software.
This software is free.
Hurry, the movie's starting!
Eat it quickly before it gets cold.
Get well soon.
How long does it take to walk to the station?
I'm getting off at the next station.
Let's meet in front of the station.

en: to come to mind, to remember

ex.en: That person's name suddenly came to me.
Rainy days make me think of pajeon.
I was thinking of my mom, so I called her.
I baked cookies at home.
A coffee and a cookie, please.
Try one of these cookies.
My finger is bleeding.
I had a blood test at the hospital.
There's still some blood in the meat.

note: 무리하다 = to overdo it. Also means 'group, crowd'.

ex.en: Don't overdo it.
Doing it all in one day is too much.
That price is a bit much for me.

note: 신청하다 = to apply, to sign up.

ex.en: Did you register for classes?
Where do I sign up for membership?
I put in a vacation request at work.

note: The 'in advance' sense is a separate word: 사전 예약.

ex.en: I look up words I don't know in the dictionary.
I often use a dictionary app on my phone.
You get a discount if you book in advance.
There were tons of people in the park.
There were countless messages waiting for me.

ex.s: 수많은 노래 중에 이게 제일 좋아요.
ex.en: Out of all those songs, I like this one best.
Press this button.
Could you press five for me?
I rang the doorbell, but nobody's home.
The company is in crisis.
A crisis can become an opportunity.
Our team was in trouble in the second half.
My parents run a small restaurant.
This store is open 24 hours.
My friend runs a YouTube channel.
Is something on your mind these days?
I'm trying to decide what to eat.
I'm debating whether to move.
The kids got into a fight.
A fight broke out in front of the bar.
A small argument turned into a big fight.
Could I get one more cup?
Please pour some water into the cup.
This cup breaks easily, so be careful.
I'm studying Korean these days.
Let's study together at the library.
How's your exam studying going?
Could you give me a shoulder massage?
I got a foot massage on my trip.
My body feels lighter after the massage.
The password is four digits.

ex.s: 우리 아이가 숫자를 셀 줄 알아요.
ex.en: Our kid knows how to count.
I'm bad with numbers.

note: Formal-sounding; everyday speech often uses 팔다.

ex.en: Does this store sell umbrellas too?
Tickets are only sold online.
That model isn't sold anymore.
Is something wrong?
What are you talking about?
I don't know what you mean.
A new café opened in our neighborhood.
I like this neighborhood because it's quiet.

ex.s: 저녁 먹고 동네 한 바퀴 걸어요.
ex.en: After dinner I take a walk around the neighborhood.
I missed the bus.
Don't miss this chance.
The cup slipped out of my hand and broke.
Unlike what I expected, the test was easy.

ex.s: 언니와 달리 저는 매운 걸 못 먹어요.
ex.en: Unlike my older sister, I can't eat spicy food.
There's no other way.
Please wait just a moment.
I can speak a little Korean.
It's a bit expensive.

note: Honorific; use -(으)시- verbs and 께 with it.

ex.en: I'm going to my parents' place this weekend.
Are your parents doing well?
I call my parents often.
We sat on the grass and rested.
The grass in the yard has gotten too long.
Can I borrow some glue?
The trip cost more than I expected.
How much does the repair cost?
Shipping is free.
There was a small earthquake last night.
If there's an earthquake, get under a desk.
I felt an earthquake during my trip to Japan.
I loaded the luggage into the car.

ex.s: 트렁크에 이 상자 좀 실어 주세요.
ex.en: Please put this box in the trunk.
Can I bring my bike on the bus?
Could you take out the trash?
Where's the trash can?
Don't throw trash on the street.

en: to be caught; to be set (date)

ex.en: The thief was caught by the police.

ex.s: 낚시 갔는데 물고기가 하나도 안 잡혔어요.
ex.en: I went fishing but didn't catch a single fish.
The wedding date has been set.
Imagine a house by the beach.
I never imagined something like that.
I imagined myself ten years from now.

en: to be empty, to be free

ex.en: Is this seat free?
The fridge is completely empty.
I'm free in the afternoon.
I failed at my diet again.
It's okay if you fail.
The first bread I made was a flop.
I called customer service.
We had a lot of customers today, so it was busy.
One moment, please.
I hung a picture on the wall.
The walls in this apartment are thin.

ex.s: 벽에 기대지 마세요, 페인트가 안 말랐어요.
ex.en: Don't lean on the wall—the paint isn't dry.
Please take me to the Gangnam branch.

ex.s: 이 은행 지점은 몇 시에 닫아요?
ex.en: What time does this bank branch close?
That café has a lot of locations.
I found my way with the map on my phone.
Please show me the map.
Is our hotel on this map?
This app has a lot of users.
I forgot my username.
New users, sign up here.
My workplace is close to home.
How's your new job?
I had dinner with my coworkers.

note: Used with negatives: 그리 비싸지 않아요.

ex.en: It's not that expensive.
It's not that cold today.
I don't have that much homework.
I'm working out, so the sweat keeps pouring.
A small river flows in front of the house.
Time really flies.
Watch your step on the stairs.
Take care not to catch a cold.
Drive safely.

note: Tap water is 수돗물; faucet is 수도꼭지.

ex.en: The capital of Korea is Seoul.
What's the capital of Canada?
It was so cold the water pipes froze.
What time does that drama air?
Is today's soccer game on TV?
My friend streams live every night.
I went to Korea for the first time last year.
It feels colder than last year.
We moved last summer.
I sent you a message—did you see it?
Please leave a voice message.
I wrote a short message in the birthday card.

ex.s: 버스 위치를 실시간으로 볼 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can see where the bus is in real time.
I watched the game live.
Let me check the current weather.
The apples are 1,000 won each.
Please wrap the gifts individually.
The kids each have their own room.

note: N에 익숙하다 = to be used to N.

ex.en: I've gotten used to life in Korea now.
This voice sounds familiar.
I'm not used to my new phone yet.
I'm going to see a musical this weekend.
Tickets for that musical sold out.
What musicals do you like?
There's water on the floor, so be careful.
In Korea, people sometimes eat sitting on the floor.
There's sugar left at the bottom of the cup.
How much is it all together?
I finished all my homework.
This is all the money I have.
Please come right now.
I don't need it right away.
I'm so hungry I want to eat something right now.

note: 주의하다 = to be careful, watch out for.

ex.en: The floor is slippery, so be careful.
Be sure to read the precautions.
Watch out for pickpockets on the bus.
That movie is so sad.
I was sad because my friend moved away.
Why the sad face?
Our team kept attacking in the second half.

ex.s: 그 개는 사람을 공격할 수도 있어요.
ex.en: That dog might attack people.
In the game, attack that castle first.
The new album comes out next week.
The test scores will be released tomorrow.
I finally introduced my girlfriend to my friends.

note: N에 약하다 = to be bad at, sensitive to N.

ex.en: I don't handle the cold well.
The Wi-Fi signal is weak.
I was sickly as a kid.
We'd like to pay separately, please.
Please put the sauce on the side.
I live apart from my parents.
My flight was canceled because of the typhoon.
They say a typhoon is coming this weekend.
A typhoon's coming, so don't go outside.

note: Mild and often playful, but can still sting.

ex.en: I feel so stupid.
I stupidly left my wallet at home.
The main character in that movie is a kindhearted fool.

en: to watch (closely), to keep an eye on

ex.en: I watched the kids play.
Let's wait and see a little longer.

ex.s: 의사 선생님이 좀 더 지켜보자고 하셨어요.
ex.en: The doctor said to keep an eye on it a bit longer.
My family means the most to me.
This is a precious ring my grandmother gave me.
Thank you for taking the time.

en: to carry out, to host (a show)

ex.en: I'll run the meeting.
We're doing this project next month.
Who hosts this radio show?
Sunday mornings are really peaceful.
The kids are asleep, so there's finally peace at home.
A toast to world peace!
That actor is in a new drama.

ex.s: 제 친구가 TV 퀴즈 쇼에 출연했어요.
ex.en: My friend was on a TV quiz show.
Who's in this movie?
